title: VMF guest script output
description: The single JSON object every guest script emits on stdout. The engine parses nothing else.

schema.description: vmf.guest/3 (VERIFY-FP-1) declares the Instance Metadata Service facts; vmf.guest/4 (CLUSTER-DETECT-1) declares the cluster facts; vmf.guest/5 (ORACLE-UEK-UPDATE-1) declares uekRepositories; vmf.guest/6 (KERNEL-OFFER-EDGES-1, KERNEL-FLOOR-UPLOAD-1) declares releaseverLock and kernelPackageVersion; vmf.guest/7 (VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1) declares the facts of the unmanaged network setting. A v2 to v6 output is a valid v7 one without them.

result.description: READY/NEEDS_PREP/BLOCKED for checks; FIXED/NO_CHANGE/BLOCKED for fixes; PASS/FAIL for validations

error.description: Fatal error detail when result is BLOCKED/FAIL

facts.description: GUEST-2: what the machine REPORTED, as declared fields the engine judges - never a verdict. Before v2 these travelled as checks named 'fact:<name>', which was a convention rather than a contract: nothing declared which facts existed, so a guest could omit one and nothing noticed. That is exactly how every Windows machine came to report an UNKNOWN driver state - the Windows guest emitted no os fact and the engine fell back to guessing from a caption string. Closed on purpose: an undeclared or misspelled fact is now a validation failure instead of a silent absence.

os.description: 'Windows' or 'Linux'. Stated by the guest so the engine never infers it from an OS caption.

kernelVersion.description: Linux kernel release, as uname -r reports it.

fabric.description: The network fabric the guest currently sees - 'mana', 'mlx5', or empty. Judged against the PLAN'S TARGET, never taken as the answer on its own (DRIVER-1).

driverVersion.description: Network driver version as the guest reports it. Recorded, not judged: Microsoft publishes no minimum for Windows or for Mellanox.

vfTraffic.description: Whether accelerated-path packet counters are moving - the only proof accelerated networking is really in use.

ioTimeout.description: stornvme IoTimeoutValue per ControlSet, as 'ControlSet001=240 ControlSet002=240'. One flat fact because a declared contract cannot describe names it cannot know in advance.

ioTimeoutBefore.description: The same, as found BEFORE the post-boot repair - the evidence that the first NVMe boot resets it.

imdsReached.description: VERIFY-FP-1: whether the Instance Metadata Service answered. It answers only on the primary interface and primary IP with DHCP, so an answer proves the part of the network a move rebuilds. Judged before against after, never alone.

imdsVmSize.description: VERIFY-FP-1: the size the Instance Metadata Service says this machine is on, read from inside the guest.

imdsSecurityType.description: VERIFY-FP-1: securityProfile.securityType, for example TrustedLaunch. Recorded, not judged.

clusterService.description: CLUSTER-DETECT-1 (Windows): the ClusSvc service - running, installed and not running, or not installed. The engine judges it (Get-VmfClusterNodeVerdict).

clusterKey.description: CLUSTER-DETECT-1 (Windows): whether the registry key HKLM\Cluster is present.

sqlHadr.description: CLUSTER-DETECT-1: a SQL Server instance has HADR_Enabled set to 1 (Windows registry), or hadr.hadrenabled is 1 in /var/opt/mssql/mssql.conf (Linux). It names the kind of cluster in the reason, and never decides the block.

pacemaker.description: CLUSTER-DETECT-1 (Linux): what systemctl is-active pacemaker says, for example active or inactive.

corosync.description: CLUSTER-DETECT-1 (Linux): what systemctl is-active corosync says, for example active or inactive.

uekRepositories.description: ORACLE-UEK-UPDATE-1 (Oracle Linux only): the ids of the enabled repositories whose id has UEK in it, read from /etc/yum.repos.d, separated by one space, for example 'ol9_UEKR7 ol9_UEKR8'; 'none' when no such repository is enabled; 'unknown' when the folder cannot be read. The engine runs Update the kernel for a UEK kernel below UEK R8 only when the UEK R8 repository of the release is in this list (Resolve-VmfKernelUpdate).

releaseverLock.description: KERNEL-OFFER-EDGES-1 (Red Hat, Alma, Rocky, CentOS and Oracle Linux only): the first line of /etc/dnf/vars/releasever, else /etc/yum/vars/releasever, for example '9.4' - the minor release dnf is held to (Microsoft: the EUS, SAP and HA RHUI clients lock it); 'none' when neither file is there. The engine does not run Update the kernel where this minor release is below the release whose kernel Microsoft lists for MANA (Get-VmfKernelUpdateReach).

kernelPackageVersion.description: KERNEL-FLOOR-UPLOAD-1 (Ubuntu and Debian only): the version of the package of the running kernel, dpkg-query -W -f='${Version}' linux-image-$(uname -r), for example '5.15.0-1096.105'. Ubuntu's uname -r has no upload number, and Microsoft's minimum has one, so the engine compares this version where uname equals the minimum as far as its numbers go (Get-VmfDriverJudgement); 'unknown' when dpkg-query gives none.

networkManager.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): what systemctl is-active NetworkManager says.

networkd.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): what systemctl is-active systemd-networkd says.

wicked.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): what systemctl is-active wicked says. Recorded, not judged: Microsoft gives no unmanaged setting for it.

ifupdown.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): yes when /etc/network/interfaces or interfaces.d has an iface stanza for an interface other than lo. Recorded, not judged.

systemdVersion.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): the version number systemctl --version gives, or unknown. systemd-networkd 255 or later reads ID_NET_MANAGED_BY.

cloudInitVersion.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): the version cloud-init --version gives (for example 23.4.4), none when cloud-init is not installed, or unknown.

cloudInitNetwork.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): disabled when network-config=disabled is on the kernel command line or a cloud.cfg file holds config: disabled; then cloud-init applied no network configuration.

sriovUdevLines.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): each udev rule line in force, not a comment, that names NM_UNMANAGED, ID_NET_MANAGED_BY or AZURE_UNMANAGED_SRIOV, as '<file>: <line>', joined by ' ;; '; none when there is no line.

sriovNetworkFiles.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): each systemd .network file in force that holds Property=AZURE_UNMANAGED_SRIOV=1 and Unmanaged=yes, joined by ' ;; '; none when there is no file.

nmUnmanagedDevices.description: VF-UNMANAGED-CONFIG-1 (Linux): each unmanaged-devices value of NetworkManager, as '<file>: <value>', joined by ' ;; '; none when there is no value.
